A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseVLM study despite the changed title. The text, equations, Tables 1–14, Figures 1–11, and Appendices A–E support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original dense prediction experiments, downstream detection and segmentation results, scaling experiments, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1, 7, and 8 and supplementary experiments in Tables 10–14.

M1.justification: DenseVLM retains the same region sampling, category retrieval, denoising, decoupled alignment, and KL-divergence objective. Additional diagram labels and wording edits do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO, ADE20K, COCO-Stuff, PASCAL Context, OV-COCO, and OV-LVIS coverage, alongside SA-1B training subsets. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables and ablations. Table 1 retains OpenCLIP, DFN, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, RegionCLIP, FineCLIP, and CLIPSelf; the newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The data splits, model configurations, training budgets, image resolutions, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Both retain Top-1/Top-5 classification accuracy, segmentation mIoU, and the same detection AP metrics.

E4.justification: Both retain the same analyses of framework design, decoupling, category sets, retrieval models, data scale, backbones, image resolution, region proposals, and denoising thresholds. The confusion matrices and qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The existing point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–14 and the experimental figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DenseVLM's COCO Top-1 box, thing-mask, and stuff-mask accuracies of 72.3, 70.1, and 44.9. Rankings and qualitative findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5), including retrieval probabilities and the alignment loss, remain unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims about mitigating foreground bias, improving downstream tasks, and scaling with unlabeled data remain the same. The conclusion's revised statement about directly replacing original VLMs already appears in both abstracts.

C2.justification: The explanations of foreground bias, decoupling, scaling behavior, and experimental tradeoffs are retained. Appendix A preserves the same limitations concerning computational resources, teacher-model capacity, and fine-grained semantics.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware specifications, training details, dataset descriptions, and the code-access statement are unchanged. The new supercomputing-center acknowledgment credits support without adding experimental specifications.

R1.justification: v3 adds 11 references, including DINOv2 Meets Text, CLIP-SP, PromptKD, and vision-language surveys. These broaden citations in the introduction and related work without substantively revising DenseVLM's positioning or comparisons with prior approaches.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Unbiased Region-Language Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Dense Prediction' to 'DenseVLM: A Retrieval and Decoupled Alignment Framework for Open-Vocabulary Dense Prediction.' v3 also adds acknowledgments and makes limited wording and cross-reference edits; the section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds 'Align' labels to previously unlabeled alignment arrows. Pagination changes move appendix material and split the bibliography around Figures 7–11. All figures and tables are retained, with no substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: Extra Figure 2 labels and cross-references provide small clarity gains, while the revised pagination interrupts the bibliography with appendix figures. The added citations do not develop the research argument, and the method, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These limited presentation tradeoffs leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
